title: Friedman translation with protected first-order parameters

based_on.title: Friedman’s A-Translation (October 27, 1992)
based_on.pages: §4 pp.4–5, Definition/Lemma6, eigenvariable warning; §5 pp.5–6 only for the explicit boundary to unadopted arithmetic work

summary: Protect formula parameters beneath binders and transform actual native intuitionistic proofs, including equality and finite axiom supports.
abstract: A formula inserted inside a quantifier can accidentally acquire a new bound variable. This makes a first-order extension of Friedman translation more delicate than its propositional version. We keep each inserted parameter free of the new bound slot and construct a transformation of actual intuitionistic proof trees, including equality replacement. The raw construction needs an available term to build translated existential conclusions; public certificates supply one from their auxiliary names. Tracking every changed assumption then gives a transformation of finitely supported theory proofs and explains why preserving the original arithmetic axioms requires an additional argument.
